big: Meena's mother wrote a note on a plain page saying 'my flat goes to my daughter'. She signed it but no one else did. When she passed away, her sons disputed it. A will needs a few simple steps to stand firm.

lines: Do I need a lawyer to make a will?
Not by law, but a lawyer helps you avoid mistakes. The key steps are simple: write it clearly, sign it in front of two witnesses, and name someone to carry it out.

rows: A legal declaration of who gets what after your death
The person named to carry out the will
At least two people who see you sign, and sign too
A supplement that changes or adds to an existing will
note: Registering a will is not compulsory, but it can make it harder to dispute. A lawyer can guide you on your own case.

title: Wills
stops: A will is a legal declaration of who gets what
An executor carries out the instructions in a will
A will can never be changed once it is written
caps: It states in writing who should receive which assets.
The law requires at least two witnesses who see the maker sign.
The executor sees that the will is followed.
A codicil changes or adds to a will, and you can also write a new will.

q: Rohan wants to make a will. Which step is needed for it to be valid?
opts: Printing it on stamp paper only
Paying a fee to the bank
why: The law needs at least two witnesses who watch him sign and sign too.
Telling neighbours is not required and may even cause disputes.
Stamp paper is not what makes a will valid. The signing and witnessing are.
A bank does not validate a will, and no such fee is needed.

q: Meena names her friend to carry out her will. What is the friend called?
why: A nominee is named to receive an asset held with a bank or fund.
A witness only watches the signing and does not carry out the will.
An executor is named in a will to carry out its instructions.
A surveyor assesses an insurance loss and has no role in a will.

q: Dadi opens a new bank account after writing her will. How can she bring it in?
opts: Do nothing, since the bank will know
Add a codicil, or write a fresh will
Cross out lines on the old will at random
why: A bank does not read her will and cannot add the account.
A codicil or a fresh will brings the new account into her wishes.
An oral word to a stranger has no legal effect on the will.
Random changes can confuse the document and cause disputes.

q: Why might a person ask a lawyer to help draft a will?
opts: Because the law bans writing it alone
Because a lawyer becomes the heir
Because a will needs a court order first
To avoid errors that could lead to disputes
why: The law does not ban writing it alone, but help lowers errors.
A lawyer does not become an heir by helping to draft a will.
A will does not need a court order to be made at all.
A lawyer can spot gaps that families end up fighting over.

pts: A will states who gets what, and needs two witnesses.
The executor carries out the will. A codicil changes it.
A lawyer helps avoid mistakes. Update the will after big changes.
